passage:
Since Asif's promotion at the district cooperative office, Karthik's replies had shrunk to single words, and at the tea stall Karthik kept looking at the road. Asif felt awkward and lonely. He had stopped talking about work, afraid of sounding proud, and the silence had made things stiffer.

One Sunday at the temple fair, Asif said, "I was scared of bragging, so I said nothing about the new job. It's just a bigger desk. How is the shop going?" Karthik shrugged, then said, "Slow. The wholesaler raised prices."

They talked for an hour by the ring-toss stall. "It's odd," Karthik said, "watching you move up while I'm still counting stock." Asif didn't defend himself. "That sounds hard. I'd feel it too." Karthik grinned a little.

qa.q: Where did Asif and Karthik talk for an hour?
qa.a: They talked by the ring-toss stall at the temple fair.

qa.q: How does Asif feel about Karthik's coldness?
qa.a: Awkward and lonely; Asif stopped talking about work for fear of sounding proud.

qa.q: What worked in how Asif approached Karthik?
qa.a: Asif shared briefly without bragging, asked about Karthik's shop, and listened without defending himself.

qa.q: What might Karthik be feeling as Asif moves up?
qa.a: Karthik seems to feel behind, counting stock while Asif advances, and may have pulled away because of that sting.

grounding: A friend turns cold after Asif's promotion; Asif shares his life without bragging, asks about theirs, and makes it safe to stay friends.

passage:
At the insurance office in Kochi, Joseph's new nameplate said Team Lead. Vikas, who had joined the same week three years ago, now sat two desks away and barely said good morning.

In the pantry, Joseph tried. "Chai?" "I'm fine." Vikas left with his bottle.

Joseph felt awkward and oddly lonely. He hadn't changed. But he could see how the nameplate looked from Vikas's chair.

That Friday he didn't mention the promotion or the new targets. He found Vikas at the bike stand. "How's your mother's knee after the surgery?"

Vikas blinked. "Better. She's walking to the church again."

"That's great. And your running? You were training for the half marathon."

"Still am. Twenty kilometres last Sunday."

"Madman," Joseph said. Vikas almost smiled. On Monday he said good morning first, and on Wednesday they had chai together, talking about anything but work.

qa.q: What did Joseph's new nameplate say?
How did Joseph feel when Vikas turned down the chai?
qa.a: Joseph felt awkward and oddly lonely, sensing their friendship cooling.

qa.q: What did Joseph do to keep the friendship safe?
qa.a: He stopped talking about the promotion and asked about Vikas's mother and running, showing real interest in his life.

qa.q: How might Vikas see Joseph's promotion?
qa.a: Vikas probably feels envious and left behind, since they joined together and now Joseph leads the team.

grounding: The passage shows a young man whose friend has gone cold since his promotion, feeling awkward and lonely, who asks about his friend's life without bragging.

passage:
Dear Ganga,

It's been two months since my wedding, and I've noticed you've gone quiet. You held my dupatta when I was a shaking bride, and then you left the reception early, and you haven't answered my last three messages. I might be wrong. But I think something changed between us, and I miss you.

I know my messages lately have been all about the wedding, the new house, Faraz's family. That must have been a lot to scroll through. I'm sorry if it felt like I was showing off. I wasn't trying to.

I want to hear about you. How is the job at the library? Did you ever finish that mural in your room? Is your mother still making those terrible experimental pickles?

Marriage hasn't replaced you. You were my first friend in this city, my sister in everything but blood, and you still are. You can tell me anything, including that you're annoyed with me.

Tea at our old place, Saturday at four?

Noor

qa.q: How many of Noor's messages has Ganga not answered?
qa.a: Ganga hasn't answered the last three messages.

qa.q: How does Noor feel about Ganga going quiet?
qa.a: Noor feels awkward and lonely, missing Ganga and worried something changed between them.

qa.q: What makes Noor's letter a good way to reach Ganga?
qa.a: It admits Noor's messages were full of wedding news, asks warmly about Ganga's life, and makes it safe for Ganga to say she's annoyed.

qa.q: How might Ganga have felt scrolling through Noor's wedding messages?
qa.a: Ganga may have felt left behind and a little envious, as if Noor's new life had no room for her.

grounding: A letter shows a young woman whose friend has gone cold since her marriage, sharing her life without bragging and asking about her friend's so the friendship feels safe.
